title: Introduce adaptive request sharding and cache adapter cohesion to reduce Console tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Reduce 95th/99th percentile tail latency for the Console API aggregation and GraphQL resolvers by refactoring request routing and unifying cache adapter semantics. Background: Console serves high-fanout dashboards where hot endpoints cause noisy neighbors and cache stampedes. Current symptoms include spikes during tenant bursts, inconsistent cache TTLs across adapters, and duplicated fetches across GraphQL and REST layers. Goals: 1) Introduce adaptive request sharding so long-lived aggregation work is distributed to a bounded worker pool; 2) Replace ad-hoc cache adapters with a small compatibility layer that enforces prefix semantics, single-source TTL smoothing, and read-through coalescing; 3) Remove duplicate fetch paths between GraphQL resolvers and REST adapters; 4) Provide telemetry and contention metrics to verify improvement. Success metrics: 25-40% reduction in p95 for dashboard endpoints, 50% fewer duplicate upstream fetches, and measurable reduction in CPU/memory spikes under burst load. Constraints: must be zero-downtime and compatible with Dedicated deployments where some cache adapters are sharded differently. Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary on 10% of traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> global, with auto-rollback on SLO regressions. Testing: synthetic load harness in staging (k6 + recorded production traces), unit tests for cache adapter invariants, and perf bench PRs. Migration notes: a short migration job will standardize TTLs for existing cache entries (script in infra repo). Trade-offs considered: synchronous coalescing reduces duplicate fetches but can increase tail if worker pool saturates; chosen mitigation is adaptive admission with backoff and optimistic staleness reads for low-priority widgets.
